title: The Letter of the Lower Danube
premise: In 1912, in a river town on the Lower Danube, apprentice clockmaker Wendell Delacroix arrives to repair the observatory's failing master clock, only to find the bridge out of town closed for the season by military order. Trapped among strangers, she uncovers letters hidden inside the clock's case — a wartime promise between her late master and a man now declared an enemy officer across the river. As the town's suspicion sharpens and the clock's mechanism fails faster than she can mend it, Wendell must choose between the silence that has kept her safe and the found family forming around her. She repairs the clock, delivers the letter through the frozen crossing at great cost, and learns that keeping time means knowing when to break it.
about_author: Casper Eriksen is the pen name of a former restorer of antique clocks who spent a decade working along the Danube's river towns before turning to fiction. Their novels are known for quiet tension, mechanical detail, and characters who love more bravely than they speak.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Wendell travels downriver to the observatory town, carrying her dead master's tools and a habit of making herself small. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: wary hope — a new place might finally be safe.

chapters.title: A Town That Runs Late
chapters.summary: The observatory's master clock has stopped, and with it, oddly, the town's rhythm; bells ring wrong, ferries misconnect. Wendell meets Ilinca, the observatory keeper's blunt daughter, who resents needing an outsider. POV: Wendell. Beat: first friction, first flicker of belonging.

chapters.title: What the Case Conceals
chapters.summary: Opening the clock's case, Wendell finds a sealed packet of letters wedged behind the escapement, addressed to a name she doesn't recognize — and marked with her master's seal. POV: Wendell. Beat: dread and curiosity entwined; the past has hands inside her work.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Military orders seal the bridge for the season; rumors of war move upriver like weather. Wendell realizes she cannot leave until spring. POV: Ilinca, watching the last travelers turned back. Beat: claustrophobia — the town becomes a clock case itself.

chapters.title: Letters Written in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Reading the letters, Wendell learns of a friendship between her master and Anton Varga, now an officer on the far bank — and of a promise to deliver a final letter should one of them die. POV: Wendell. Beat: grief reframed; her master had a life she never knew.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Ilinca's family folds Wendell into supper, arguments, and card games; for the first time in years she speaks without calculating the cost. POV: Ilinca, observing Wendell's guardedness begin to crack. Beat: warmth as risk.

chapters.title: Escapement
chapters.summary: Wendell diagnoses the clock's deeper fault — a cracked wheel no spare can replace — and must machine a new one by hand while the town's patience thins. POV: Wendell. Beat: competence under pressure; craft as identity.

chapters.title: The Man Who Watches the River
chapters.summary: A gendarme, Captain Sorin, begins asking why the new clockmaker reads foreign postmarks and studies the far bank. Wendell deploys her old silences. POV: Sorin, half-suspicious, half-lonely. Beat: the hunter given a human face.

chapters.title: Enemy Across the Water
chapters.summary: News arrives that Varga's regiment holds the opposite shore; delivering the letter would be treason. Ilinca discovers what Wendell carries and must decide whether to report her. POV: Ilinca. Beat: loyalty tested before it's fully formed.

chapters.title: Midnight Oiling
chapters.summary: Working nights to hide both the repair and the letters, Wendell nearly destroys the escapement; Ilinca catches her and instead helps, demanding the whole truth. POV: Wendell. Beat: confession — invisibility abandoned.

chapters.title: The Promise, Explained
chapters.summary: Ilinca's father reveals he knew of the correspondence; the two men repaired this very clock together years ago, before borders hardened. He warns Wendell what Sorin will do if he finds out. POV: the keeper. Beat: history complicating duty; the past was kinder than the present.

chapters.title: Frost on the Escapement
chapters.summary: Cold snaps; the workshop freezes, the clock stalls publicly, and the town blames its bad luck on the outsider. Wendell works feverishly as Sorin requests her papers from the capital. POV: Wendell. Beat: time running out made literal.

chapters.title: What Silence Keeps Safe
chapters.summary: Ilinca confronts Wendell about the seven years of hiding — who she was fleeing, what names she's shed. Wendell tells her, for the first time, everything. POV: alternating close. Beat: intimacy forged in honesty; love acknowledged without being named.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Debt
chapters.summary: An old ferryman who once owed Wendell's master agrees to attempt the winter crossing — once, after ice thickens enough to bear weight but before it closes completely. A narrow window. POV: the ferryman. Beat: fragile hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: Sorin's Summons
chapters.summary: Sorin detains Wendell over her irregular papers; Ilinca lies to protect her, binding their fates openly. Sorin lets her go — but posts a watch on the observatory. POV: Sorin. Beat: mercy with teeth; the net tightening.

chapters.title: The Wheel Turns
chapters.summary: Wendell finishes machining the replacement wheel; the master clock strikes true for the first time in months, and the town's goodwill briefly outweighs its suspicion. POV: Wendell. Beat: triumph shadowed by knowledge that it changes nothing about the letter.

chapters.title: Orders from the Capital
chapters.summary: Sorin receives confirmation that Wendell's master was investigated before his death; he comes to arrest her quietly. The keeper hides the letters inside the clock's case again — where they began. POV: Ilinca. Beat: terror; the found family risks itself as one body.

chapters.title: Crossing at First Light
chapters.summary: Before dawn, Wendell slips out with the letter; the ferryman takes her onto groaning ice toward the far bank as the observatory clock strikes six above the sleeping town. POV: Wendell. Beat: courage at maximum cost; no way back.

chapters.title: The Other Shore
chapters.summary: Wendell reaches Varga's outpost and delivers the letter into the hands of a tired, older man who weeps over a friend's handwriting. Soldiers take her into custody — gently, because of who vouches for her. POV: Varga. Beat: the promise kept; grief and relief in one breath.

chapters.title: Negotiation at the Clock
chapters.summary: Varga crosses under truce flag to speak with Sorin; the two officers, bound by the same dead clockmaker's story, arrange Wendell's return in exchange for discretion. POV: Sorin. Beat: enemies choosing humanity over procedure.

chapters.title: Spring Thaw
chapters.summary: The bridge reopens; Wendell could leave, and stands at its foot with her packed tools — then turns back. Ilinca is waiting at the observatory door. POV: Wendell. Beat: choosing to stay; love against every old instinct to vanish.

chapters.title: Keeping Time
chapters.summary: One year later: the clock runs, the town has adopted its clockmaker, and a new letter — friendly, unhidden — arrives across the river. Wendell oils the escapement beside Ilinca as the bells ring true. POV: Wendell. Beat: resolution — memory honored, family chosen, time finally on her side.
